learning_objective: 🎯 Become a safety hero! Learn how to prevent sports injuries, administer crucial first aid, and respond to emergencies effectively.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Injuries can be soft tissue (sprains, strains, contusions) or bone/joint injuries (fractures, dislocations). A 'sprain' is a torn ligament, while a 'strain' is a torn muscle/tendon.
Most injuries can be prevented by proper warm-up, stretching, using correct protective equipment (helmets, shin guards), following rules, and avoiding overtraining.
For soft tissue injuries, immediately apply the R.I.C.E principle: Rest, Ice (reduces swelling), Compression (wrap it), and Elevation (keep it above heart level).
Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is an emergency procedure done when someone's heartbeat or breathing stops. It involves hard, fast chest compressions to keep blood flowing to the brain.
The process of restoring an injured athlete back to full physical function through physiotherapy, exercises, and gradual return to sports.

fun_activity.title: 🧊 The R.I.C.E Drill
fun_activity.instructions: Grab a stuffed animal and pretend it sprained its ankle. Practice the R.I.C.E method on it: Have it Rest, put a fake Ice pack, wrap a bandage around it (Compression), and prop its leg up on a pillow (Elevation)!

exam_tips: 📌 Always know the difference between a Sprain (ligament) and a Strain (muscle/tendon).
📌 Be able to expand the acronyms R.I.C.E and CPR.
📌 A warm-up prepares the body physically and mentally, drastically reducing the chance of muscle tears.
quick_recap: ⭐ First Aid is the immediate and temporary care given to a victim before professional medical help arrives.
⭐ Never apply heat to a fresh injury; always use ice to control internal bleeding and swelling.
⭐ 'Dislocation' is when bones are forced out of their normal positions in a joint.
